Vendor must be capable of providing HACCP certification services
Vendor must be capable of providing ISO 22000 certification services
Vendor must have existing or demonstrated footprint in MENA and Levant regions
technical_requirements: Service delivery capability in Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, and Syria
key_constraints: Primary target: WFP country offices in Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Syria

registration_checklist: 1. Confirm UNGM Level 1 status is active and that WFP is selected as a subscribing agency in your UNGM profile (log in at https://www.ungm.org, navigate to 'My Profile' → 'Subscribing Organizations', tick WFP).

2. Navigate to the WFP Procurement portal at https://www.wfp.org/procurement and locate the 'Become a Supplier' or 'Supplier Registration' section to confirm current supplementary registration requirements for service vendors.

3. Prepare and rename all supporting documents according to the UN-friendly filename convention (see document_renaming_rules) before uploading — WFP portals flag mismatched or unlabelled files during review.

4. Log in to UNGM and update your UNSPSC category codes to include food-safety-specific codes: 70141700 (Food safety services), 85121806 (Food testing and inspection), 70141600 (Quality assurance consulting), 86101500 (Vocational training / food handler training) — remove any overly broad codes.

5. In your UNGM profile, update the 'Geographic Areas of Operation' to explicitly list Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, and Syria (even if Syria is dormant — note 'pre-2020, currently dormant' in the remarks field).
6. Draft and upload a WFP-specific Capability Statement (see capability_statement_draft) as a standalone PDF — do not rely solely on the generic company profile.

7. Prepare a Food-Safety Policy document (1-2 pages) that references HACCP principles, ISO 22000 alignment, and Codex Alimentarius standards — WFP requires food vendors to submit food-safety policies; adapt this for advisory/testing services.

8. Compile a Past Performance Summary sheet listing the USAID Lebanon CSP engagement (2020-2023) and UNDP Lebanon training-of-trainers (2022) with contract values, scope, client contact details, and outcomes — attach the USAID Reference Letter as supporting evidence.

9. Obtain a formal letter or certificate from your Tripoli ISO 17025 lab partner confirming the partnership arrangement, scope of testing services covered, and geographic reach — WFP will want to verify lab capacity is not solely self-declared.

10. Contact the WFP Lebanon Country Office procurement focal point (Beirut) directly to introduce MEFOSA and confirm whether a country-office-level supplementary registration or expression of interest is required in addition to the UNGM/portal registration.
11. Contact the WFP Jordan Country Office (Amman) procurement team similarly, referencing your 3 active clients in Jordan as evidence of in-country operational presence.
12. Upload all documents to the WFP supplier portal (or UNGM profile if WFP routes through UNGM for service vendors) and submit — retain the submission confirmation email and reference number.
13. Set a 30-day calendar reminder to follow up with both WFP Lebanon and WFP Jordan country office procurement focal points if no acknowledgement is received.

14. Monitor WFP's UNGM tender notices and the WFP procurement portal for food-safety advisory RFQs or LTA calls in Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq — respond to at least one open tender within 90 days to establish a transactional record.
output.capability_statement_draft:
MEFOSA – MENA Food Safety Associates S.A.R.L is a Beirut-headquartered food-safety advisory and laboratory-testing firm founded in 2014, delivering end-to-end food-safety solutions across Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq. With a team of four senior consultants, six field auditors, and accredited laboratory access through our ISO 17025-certified Tripoli partner, MEFOSA provides HACCP system design and implementation, ISO 22000 certification advisory, Codex Alimentarius alignment for food exporters, and microbiological and chemical laboratory testing. Our services are delivered in Arabic, English, and French, enabling direct engagement with local food producers, SMEs, and government counterparts across the Levant and broader MENA region.

MEFOSA has a demonstrated track record of delivering food-safety advisory services under donor-funded programmes, including a multi-year USAID Lebanon Country Support Programme engagement (2020–2023) supporting food-safety compliance for Lebanese SMEs, and a UNDP Lebanon training-of-trainers programme (2022) building national food-handler capacity. These engagements — totalling six sub-million-USD advisory contracts with no audit qualifications — confirm MEFOSA's ability to operate within UN and donor procurement frameworks, meet reporting requirements, and deliver measurable outcomes in complex operating environments.

Three differentiators position MEFOSA as a high-value partner for WFP country offices in the Levant: (1) Regulatory fluency — MEFOSA maintains active liaison with the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and has deep familiarity with national food-safety regulatory frameworks across Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq, enabling rapid contextualisation of international standards for local food-system actors; (2) Accredited laboratory access — through our ISO 17025-certified Tripoli lab partner, MEFOSA can provide microbiological and chemical testing to internationally recognised standards without reliance on external referral chains; and (3) Bilingual training capacity — our Arabic-language food-safety training and training-of-trainers programmes are directly deployable to WFP-supported food-system beneficiaries, local NGO partners, and government counterparts, reducing translation and adaptation costs.

MEFOSA is registered on the UN Global Marketplace (UNGM ID 454934) and holds a clean 2024 audit from BDO Lebanon. We are actively seeking to register on the WFP supplier database to support WFP Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq country offices with food-safety advisory, HACCP implementation, food-handler training, and laboratory-testing services aligned with WFP's food-safety and quality assurance requirements.

Annual Turnover: BDO audited financials (2022–2024) should be used to populate financial capacity fields. If WFP portal asks for a single annual revenue figure, use the most recent audited year (2024). Do not self-declare figures not supported by the BDO audit.

output.cover_letter_draft:
Dear WFP Procurement Team,

MEFOSA – MENA Food Safety Associates S.A.R.L (UNGM ID: 454934) respectfully submits this registration package for inclusion in the WFP supplier database under the Services category, specifically for food-safety advisory, HACCP implementation, ISO 22000 certification advisory, and food-handler training services. Headquartered in Beirut, Lebanon, with active client engagements in Jordan and Iraq, MEFOSA has delivered food-safety advisory and training programmes under USAID and UNDP-funded projects since 2014, working directly with food-system SMEs, government counterparts, and local NGO partners across the Levant. Our ISO 17025-accredited laboratory partner in Tripoli enables us to provide microbiological and chemical food-safety testing to internationally recognised standards in support of WFP food-safety and quality assurance requirements.

We are committed to WFP's procurement principles of transparency, accountability, and value for money, and we hold a clean 2024 audit from BDO Lebanon. We are actively engaged with WFP Lebanon and WFP Jordan country offices and are prepared to respond rapidly to requests for food-safety advisory, HACCP gap assessments, food-handler training-of-trainers programmes, and laboratory testing services. We welcome the opportunity to support WFP's food-safety and quality assurance objectives across Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq, and we are available for any clarification or pre-qualification discussion at the procurement team's convenience.
submission_guidance: WFP does not maintain a fully open self-registration portal for service vendors in the same way UNGM does — confirm the current registration pathway at https://www.wfp.org/procurement before uploading documents, as the process may route through UNGM for service categories.

UNGM visibility to WFP: Ensure WFP is ticked as a subscribing organization in your UNGM profile (Step 1 of checklist) — this is the primary mechanism by which WFP buyers discover service vendors. Do not assume WFP buyers search the portal proactively; they often search UNGM directly.

Common rejection reason — category mismatch: WFP buyers filter by UNSPSC code. If your codes are too broad (e.g. 70000000 Business Services) your profile will not surface in food-safety-specific searches. Use the specific codes listed in organization_profile_notes.

Common rejection reason — missing food-safety policy: WFP requires food vendors to submit a food-safety policy. Even though MEFOSA is an advisory firm (not a food supplier), submit a food-safety policy document describing your internal quality assurance methodology — this signals professionalism and reduces the risk of being filtered out.

Common rejection reason — no humanitarian-response reference: WFP procurement is emergency-response oriented. The USAID Lebanon CSP reference is strong but is a development (not humanitarian) reference. If possible, obtain a letter from UNDP Lebanon or any humanitarian-response client that references MEFOSA's ability to mobilise quickly.

Country office outreach is not optional: WFP Lebanon (Beirut) and WFP Jordan (Amman) country offices procure locally and often do not rely on the global portal for service vendors. Email the country office procurement focal point directly after portal submission — include your UNGM ID, a one-page capability summary, and the cover letter.

File size: WFP and UNGM portals typically enforce a 5 MB per-file limit. The BDO audited financials (3 years) may exceed this — compress the PDF or split into separate annual files (e.g. 03a_Audited_Financials_2022.pdf, 03b_Audited_Financials_2023.pdf, 03c_Audited_Financials_2024.pdf).

Do not register under 'Food Vendor' category: MEFOSA has no warehousing, fleet, or commodity supply capacity. Registering under food-supply categories will trigger a capacity verification WFP cannot confirm, leading to rejection or de-listing. Register strictly under 'Services'.

LTA opportunity: WFP Lebanon has historically issued Long-Term Agreements for food-safety advisory and training services. Monitor the WFP UNGM tender page and the WFP Lebanon country office procurement notices — an LTA converts one successful bid into 1–3 years of repeat work.

Retain all submission confirmations: Save the UNGM profile update confirmation, any WFP portal submission reference numbers, and all email correspondence with country office procurement focal points. These are required if you need to appeal a rejection or escalate a delayed review.
